html:
Solid chocolate mixed with milk, first made successfully by the Swiss chocolatier Daniel Peter in Vevey in 1875.

Chocolate had reached Europe from Mexico in the 1500s as a drink. Solid eating chocolate came only in the 1800s. Adding milk was hard because water in milk made the chocolate spoil and turn grainy. Peter worked on the problem for years and solved it with condensed milk made by his neighbour in Vevey, Henri Nestlé, whose company later took over the brand.

Other Swiss makers improved chocolate further. In 1879 Rodolphe Lindt invented conching, long stirring that made chocolate smooth. Swiss milk chocolate became famous across the world and built a large export industry. British makers followed, with Cadbury's Dairy Milk in 1905. Milk chocolate is now the most eaten kind, and its demand drives cocoa farming in West Africa, where the crop arrived in the late 1800s.
sum: Solid chocolate mixed with milk, first made successfully by the Swiss chocolatier Daniel Peter in Vevey in 1875.
